simple.meaning: חָסַם (châçam) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to muzzle ; by analogy, to stop the nose.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Deuteronomy, Ezekiel, beginning at Deuteronomy 25:4. The surrounding contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָסַם (H2629) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָסַם (châçam) / H2629 is traced through Deuteronomy 25:4, Ezekiel 39:11 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to muzzle ; by analogy, to stop the nose
definitions.full: H2629. chasam [ חָסַם ] verb stop up, muzzle (Late Hebrew id. , חסום muzzle ; Aramaic חֲסַם bind up fast ) — Qal Imperfect בְּדִישׁוֺ שׁוֺר תַחְסֹם לֹא Deut 25:4 thou shalt not muzzle an ox when it is treading (i.e. threshing); Participle היא וְחֹסֶמֶת Ezek 39:11 and it shall stop (the way of) the passers-by; but read אתהַֿגַּיְא וְחָֽסְמוּ and they shall stop up the valley , Co see ᵐ5 Syrver Hi.

occurrences.englishText: You shall not muzzle the ox when he treads out the grain.

“ ‘ “It will happen in that day, that I will give to Gog a place for burial in Israel, the valley of those who pass through on the east of the sea; and it will stop those who pass through. They will bury Gog and all his multitude there; and they will call it ‘The valley of Hamon Gog’.
